title: Drift Wood #30 · the Crab Derby, ii
logline: Fifteenth annual. The uncle wants the same crab. Wood wants to grow.

panels.composition: The shack. Last year's flyer still on the wall, weathered. The UNCLE tapping it.

balloons.text: Same crab. Change the number. Fifteen.

image.prompt: an older fisherman tapping a weathered year-old flyer with a large crab on a shingle shack wall, two teenagers beside him

balloons.text: An artist doesn't repeat himself. This year the crab could be seen from below. Looming. A crab of consequence.

image.prompt: a teenage boy in an overcoat with a hand to his chest, wounded, proposing something to a fisherman

panels.composition: The uncle. Gully, behind him, shaking his head at Wood: don't.

image.prompt: a fisherman's flat face with a boy in a backwards cap behind him shaking his head in warning

panels.composition: The new flyer beside the old one. The same crab, exactly, but the hatching is finer, the shadow deeper, the number says 15. Only Gully notices it's better.

characters.pose: looking closely at the two flyers

image.prompt: two nearly identical crab flyers side by side on a shingle wall, the newer one more finely hatched, a boy in a backwards cap leaning in to compare them

notes: The second commission. Same crab, better. The pattern of the whole life, in a flyer.
